## Purpose
`GET /api/status` reports whether the platform is up, as the signed-in caller sees it in their workspace.

## Responsibilities
- Returns `health.user_status(workspace_id of the current principal, or None)`.
- The response contains `status` (operational, degraded or outage), `headline`, `components` and `issues`, in plain language with no internal details.

## Key elements
`system_status()`.

## Control flow
None.

## Data, state and side effects
None of its own; the health results are cached for 15 s.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- Route policy: ANY, so a signed-in user or an admin may call it.
- The frontend status indicator polls it every `UI_HEALTH_POLL_SECONDS`.

## Error handling and edge cases
None.

## Nuances and gotchas
An admin has no workspace, so for an admin no worker check is included.

## How to rebuild this file
One router with one GET handler.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_health.py`.
